sources.title: US stops visitor visas for people from Gaza

supported_event_claim: The State Department announced that it was halting visitor visas for people from Gaza while it conducted a review.
reason: Reuters directly reports the State Department announcement and its stated review; AP independently reports the same visa halt and dates the report to August 17, 2025.

sources.title: Trump interrupts talks with European leaders to call Putin, says EU diplomat

supported_event_claim: During talks in Washington with European leaders, President Trump interrupted the talks to telephone Russian President Vladimir Putin.
reason: Reuters directly reports the phone call and the interruption of the European-leader talks, citing an EU diplomat.

sources.title: Trump’s pick to lead BLS ran Twitter account full of bigoted attacks

supported_event_claim: CNN reported that E.J. Antoni, President Trump’s nominee to lead the Bureau of Labor Statistics, operated a since-deleted Twitter account containing sexually degrading attacks, derogatory remarks about gay people, conspiracy theories and insults aimed at Trump critics.
reason: CNN directly describes its reporting on the nominee’s since-deleted account and the categories of posts it found; the source supports the account and content claims without establishing motive or wrongdoing.

sources.title: Trump vows to end use of mail-in ballots ahead of 2026 midterm election

supported_event_claim: President Trump said he would pursue an executive order to end the use of mail-in ballots and voting machines ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
reason: Reuters directly reports Trump’s August 18 pledge and quotes his stated intention to eliminate mail-in ballots and voting machines; it also notes that legal experts disputed presidential authority to order such changes.

sources.title: Gabbard abruptly ousted CIA Russia expert days after Trump-Putin meeting

supported_event_claim: On August 19, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearance of a CIA officer described as a senior Russia expert, effectively ending the officer’s access to classified work.
reason: CNN and The Washington Post directly report the officer’s clearance revocation and identify the timing as days after the Trump-Putin Alaska summit; the Post also reports that Gabbard’s memo said the revocation was directed at Trump’s direction.

sources.title: Trump targets the Smithsonian again, says it focuses too much on 'how bad slavery was'

supported_event_claim: On August 19, 2025, Trump wrote that the Smithsonian focused excessively on how bad slavery was and said he would pressure the institution through a review.
reason: Reuters directly reports and quotes Trump's August 19 social-media statement and places it in the context of the White House review of Smithsonian museums.

sources.title: Why did Tulsi Gabbard fire the NSA's chief data scientist?

supported_event_claim: Reporting said DNI Tulsi Gabbard revoked the security clearance of, and thereby removed from duty, NSA chief data scientist Vinh Nguyen during the week of August 18, 2025.
reason: The fetched MS NOW report identifies Nguyen as the NSA's chief data scientist and quotes contemporaneous New York Times reporting that Gabbard revoked his clearance and fired him; it does not independently establish the editorialized allegation about conspiracy theories.

sources.title: RFK Jr. Vowed to Find the Environmental Causes of Autism. Then He Shut Down Research Trying to Do Just That.

supported_event_claim: ProPublica reported that HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. eliminated a NIOSH division studying environmental factors related to autism and that more than 50 autism-related studies lost funding.
reason: The directly fetched contemporaneous ProPublica investigation documents both the division's elimination and funding reductions, while also noting that Kennedy announced a new autism research initiative; it does not establish that all autism research was shut down.

sources.title: Top US spy Gabbard announces staff cut of over 40% from her office

supported_event_claim: On August 20, 2025, DNI Tulsi Gabbard announced a plan to reduce personnel in the Office of the Director of National Intelligence by more than 40% by October 1.
reason: Reuters directly reports Gabbard's announced personnel reduction. The source does not establish the broader characterization that the intelligence community was 'gutted' or that the plan opened the door to foreign election meddling.

sources.title: Trump says U.S. will not approve solar or wind power projects

supported_event_claim: On August 20, 2025, Trump said his administration would not approve wind or solar power projects.
reason: The directly fetched CNBC report quotes Trump's statement and describes it as a policy declaration; it also distinguishes the statement from the administration's separate changes to federal permitting.

sources.title: US prolongs Michigan coal plant's operation until November despite costs

supported_event_claim: The U.S. Energy Department extended an order requiring the J.H. Campbell coal plant in West Olive, Michigan, to remain open through November 19, 2025.
reason: Reuters directly reported the Energy Department's August 21 extension, identified the plant and location, and gave the November 19 end date.

sources.title: US Supreme Court lets Trump cut diversity-related NIH grants

supported_event_claim: The Supreme Court, by a 5-4 vote, allowed the Trump administration to proceed with terminations of certain National Institutes of Health research grants while the legal challenge continued.
reason: Reuters directly reported the Court's August 21 order, vote, and effect on NIH grant terminations; it did not establish the editorialized characterization beyond those facts.

sources.title: Russian attack on western Ukraine hits an American factory during the US-led push for peace

supported_event_claim: Russia launched a drone and missile attack on western Ukraine that struck targets including an American-owned electronics plant, according to Ukrainian officials cited by AP.
reason: AP directly reported the overnight August 21 attack and the strike on the American-owned plant; it did not establish any claim about Trump's personal statement or motive.

sources.title: In latest purge, Hegseth removes head of Pentagon intelligence agency, other senior commanders

supported_event_claim: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed the head of the Defense Intelligence Agency and ordered the removal of the chief of the U.S. Naval Reserve and the commander of Naval Special Warfare Command; Reuters reported that the reasons were unknown.
reason: Reuters directly reported the three removals on August 22 and attributed the information to U.S. officials, while explicitly stating that the reasons were not known.

sources.title: US to take 10% equity stake in Intel, in Trump's latest corporate move

supported_event_claim: Intel announced an agreement under which the U.S. government would purchase 433.3 million Intel shares for an approximately 9.9% stake, funded through specified government grants.
reason: Reuters reported the announced 10% government stake, and Intel's contemporaneous release directly specified the 433.3 million shares and 9.9% ownership percentage.

sources.title: FBI agents search Trump critic Bolton's home in latest move against rival

supported_event_claim: FBI agents searched John Bolton's home in Bethesda, Maryland, and an FBI spokesperson confirmed court-authorized activity in the area as part of a national-security probe.
reason: Reuters directly reported the search on August 22 and attributed confirmation of court-authorized activity to an FBI spokesperson.

sources.title: Pictured: Trump's hand covered in heavy makeup

supported_event_claim: Donald Trump was photographed with what The Telegraph described as a heavy layer of makeup on his right hand.
reason: The contemporaneous Telegraph report, published August 22, includes and describes a photograph showing makeup on Trump's right hand; it does not establish a cause or medical explanation.

sources.title: US orders Orsted to halt offshore wind project, deepening industry woes

supported_event_claim: The Trump administration ordered Orsted to stop construction on the Revolution Wind offshore project near Rhode Island, which Reuters reported was 80% complete.
reason: Reuters directly reported the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management stop-work order and the project's reported 80% completion on August 22.

sources.title: Trump threatens to send the military to Baltimore to 'clean up' crime

supported_event_claim: On August 24, Trump said that he would send troops to Baltimore if Maryland Governor Wes Moore wanted help.
reason: NBC News directly reported Trump's August 24 statement and quoted his post referring to sending troops to Baltimore.

sources.title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Imposes Measures to End Cashless Bail and Enforce the Law in Washington, D.C.

supported_event_claim: Trump signed an executive order on August 25 directing steps intended to end or limit cashless bail in Washington, D.C.
reason: The White House fact sheet confirms the signing and its stated D.C. objective, while Reuters independently reported the signing and described the order's intended effect.

sources.title: As it happened: Trump orders firing of Fed governor Lisa Cook

supported_event_claim: President Donald Trump said on August 25 that he was firing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook; Cook disputed the action and said she would challenge it.
reason: Reuters directly reported Trump's firing announcement, Cook's response, and the Federal Reserve's indication that her status remained unchanged pending legal resolution.

sources.title: Additional Measures To Address the Crime Emergency in the District of Columbia

supported_event_claim: An August 25 executive order directed the creation and training of specialized public-safety units, including a specialized unit within the District of Columbia National Guard subject to Title 32 activation.
reason: The official executive-order text directly documents the order and its provisions; it does not establish the editorialized characterization that the units were intended to 'crush civil unrest.'

sources.title: Prosecuting Burning of The American Flag

supported_event_claim: Trump signed an August 25 executive order directing federal enforcement and prosecution of certain laws involving flag desecration and directing litigation concerning the First Amendment's scope.
reason: The White House order and contemporaneous Reuters report directly verify that the order was signed and describe its directives. The sources do not establish that Trump admitted the order violated the First Amendment; Reuters instead reports that the order prompted free-speech concerns and that Supreme Court precedent protects flag burning as expression.

sources.title: Trump says China has to give US magnets or face 200% tariff

supported_event_claim: Trump told reporters that China would face a possible 200% tariff if it did not provide the United States with magnets.
reason: Reuters directly reported the August 25 statement and quoted Trump's conditional reference to a 200% tariff amid the trade dispute.

sources.title: Fired CDC director clashed with Kennedy on vaccine policy

supported_event_claim: Reuters reported that CDC Director Susan Monarez was fired on August 27 after resisting vaccine-policy changes advanced by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., according to a close associate.
reason: The Reuters report directly verifies the dismissal and reports the associate's account of Monarez's resistance to vaccine-policy changes. It does not specifically establish the editorialized wording that she was fired for refusing to 'limit vaccine access.'
